en.title: Do early tumor measurements improve prediction of subsequent survival?
en.summary: A patient-separated landmark analysis of public colorectal cancer data, including calibration, censoring, uncertainty and temporal-integrity sensitivity.
key_findings: In a public 150-patient colorectal-cancer subset, a week-16 landmark analysis (128 patients) used only tumor measurements available before the prediction time.
Adding early tumor change raised held-out concordance from 0.532 to 0.581 (difference +0.049, 95% interval −0.005 to +0.106), and calibration stayed weak (slope 0.464).
Early tumor change is a candidate for further study, not a survival surrogate or decision rule; a separate validation cohort and denser longitudinal data are needed.
